explanations.explanation: Not quite, baker. Matthew says darkness came over "…all the land." That's no spotlight on one hill. It lasted from the sixth hour until the ninth hour.

That's right, friend. Matthew says the darkness came "…over all the land." and Golgotha is only one spot in it. It stayed from the sixth hour until the ninth hour. Imagine stepping outside in the middle of the day and finding the whole sky dark.

Yes, baker. Some of those standing there heard Jesus cry "Eli, Eli" and said, "He is calling Elijah." Elijah was a prophet from long ago (1 Kings 18:36). They heard a cry in the darkness and that's the name they landed on.

Close on the history, friend, but not on the verse. Moses was Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), and Matthew never has anyone in this crowd name him. The people standing there said, "He is calling Elijah." Keep your eyes on that name.

Good name, but not the one in the verse, baker. Isaiah was a prophet (Isaiah 1:1), but Matthew doesn't report anyone saying his name here. Matthew tells us they said, "He is calling Elijah." Isaiah isn't part of this scene.

explanations.answer: Holds it up for Jesus to drink
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. One of the people standing there quickly ran and brought a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and held it up for Jesus to drink. Look at how fast he moves. Matthew says he quickly ran.

explanations.answer: Hands it over to the soldiers
explanations.explanation: Not this time, friend. Matthew never has him hand the sponge to anyone. He fills it, puts it on a reed, and holds it up for Jesus to drink. The whole job is done by that one man.

explanations.answer: Sets it down beside the cross
explanations.explanation: Nope, baker. Matthew doesn't say he sets the sponge down. The man puts it on a reed and holds it up for Jesus to drink. That reed is there so the sponge can reach Him.

Right, friend. The others said, "Leave Him alone." Then they added, "Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him." So one man brings the sponge and the others say that. I think that's a lot of opinions for one cross.
That's not what they say, baker. One man has held up the sponge, and the others say, "Leave Him alone." Matthew doesn't report anyone asking for more wine. They say they want to see if Elijah comes.
Not quite, friend. Matthew doesn't report anyone asking to bring Him down. What the others say is, "Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him." That's the answer the text gives us here.
Yes, baker. Matthew says, "The earth quaked, and the rocks were split." That happened at the moment Jesus yielded up His spirit. This was no little wobble on the counter. Even the rocks split.
No water in this one, friend. Matthew says the earth quaked, and the rocks were split. Think shaking ground, not rising water. It all happened at the moment Jesus yielded up His spirit.
No fire here, baker. Matthew says, "The earth quaked, and the rocks were split." The only things I burn are cookies, and that's on me. This was the ground itself shaking.

That's right, friend. Matthew says the tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised. "Saints" here means God's people who had died. Matthew tells us that plainly and goes on with the story.

Not carried off, baker. Nobody hauls anything away in this verse. The tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised. Matthew says raised, and that's the word to hold onto.

Other way around, friend. Matthew doesn't say anything turns to dust. He says the tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised. It's about those saints being raised.

Yes, baker. Matthew says that after Jesus' resurrection, when they had come out of the tombs, they entered the holy city and appeared to many people. Notice that the verse puts it after His resurrection. Matthew tells it just that way.

The text says otherwise, friend. Matthew writes that after Jesus' resurrection, they came out of the tombs, entered the holy city, and appeared to many people. So the answer is True. Many people saw them.

Right, baker. Matthew says they were terrified when they saw the earthquake and all that had happened. These men were guarding Jesus, and I bet a shaking earth was the last thing they expected. I think I'd have dropped my whole tray of cookies.
Not angry, friend. Matthew says the centurion and those with him were terrified. They saw the earthquake and all that had happened, and fear is what the verse gives us. Right after that, they speak.
No relief in this verse, baker. The text says they were terrified. They saw the earthquake and all that had happened. I think anybody standing on that shaking ground would feel the same.

explanations.answer: Truly this was the Son of God
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. The centurion and those with him said, "Truly this was the Son of God." Matthew doesn't say why they said it, only that they saw the earthquake and all that had happened. These were the men guarding Jesus, and that's what came out of them.

explanations.answer: Truly this was a great prophet
explanations.explanation: Not those words, baker. The centurion and those with him said, "Truly this was the Son of God." They don't call Him a prophet. They name Him as God's Son.

explanations.answer: Truly this was the King of Israel
explanations.explanation: Close, friend, but that's not what these men say. "He is the King of Israel!" was said earlier by the chief priests, who were mocking Him (Matthew 27:41-42). The centurion and those with him said, "Truly this was the Son of God." Different speakers, different words.

Yes, baker. Matthew says they had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him. They came all the way from Galilee to serve Him, and they're still there watching. I think that tells you something about them.
That's not what the verse says, friend. Matthew says they had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him. Nothing in it says anything about bringing Him home. They came to serve Him.
Not quite, baker. Matthew says these women followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him. They followed Jesus Himself. Finding His disciples isn't the reason the verse gives.
